raw_response:
Thirty-five years on these five mu. Me and the old man do it ourselves now — the children work in the city, send a little money sometimes, but mostly it's just us. I'll tell you how I'll do it this year, same as most years really.

**The wheat**

Around the tenth day of the tenth month I'll plant, after the maize is cleared and the stalks chopped in. I'll buy seed at the village co-op — the kind everyone buys, I just ask for "the regular one." About thirty jin per mu, that's what feels right in the hand when you sow.

Before planting I'll put down compound fertilizer — three bags for the whole plot. That's what fills the cart, and old Zhang across the way does about the same. The tractor man plows for thirty yuan a mu, then we sow. If the ground is dry before the freeze, I give a winter water — it helps the roots settle.

Come spring, when the wheat greens up and starts standing at jointing, I carry the urea out — a bag and a half for the whole five mu — spread it by hand and then open the water. That's the important watering, my mother-in-law always said don't miss the jointing water. After that I water again at heading if it hasn't rained, maybe once more when the grain is filling if it's hot. Three or four waterings in spring, usually.

If I see the weeds coming up thick, I spray the cheap herbicide once, same as the neighbors. I don't spray for bugs unless I really see them — saves money.

Usually the wheat gives about eight hundred jin per mu. Some years nine, some years seven. Depends on whether the jointing water came on time and the wind at harvest.

**The maize**

After the wheat comes off in the sixth month, we have to move fast — three, four days and the new crop has to be in. No time to waste. We rent the direct-seeder with two neighbors, split the cost. Hybrid maize seed, you can't save seed anymore, has to be bought fresh every year.

At planting I put one bag of compound, two bags actually for the five mu. When the maize is knee-high — big trumpet stage we call it — I carry urea out, about a bag and a half, and sprinkle it along the rows before a rain or a watering. The maize eats hungry when it's growing fast.

Summer usually has rain, so I only water once or twice if July stays dry. Less work than wheat that way.

I spray weeds once when the maize is small, that's all. Maize gives me about nine hundred jin a mu in a normal year.

**Money**

Fertilizer prices went up a bit this spring but what can you do, we still need it. I keep maybe five hundred yuan aside for if something goes wrong — a well pump breaking, or the old man needs medicine. The rest goes into the inputs. We don't hire anyone, five mu the two of us can manage ourselves even getting older.
